clues.title: Plate: red strip on left, or blue both sides
text: Albanian licence plates either have **blue strips** on both sides or a single **red strip** on the left side.

NOTE: Albania is the only European country with red on the left side of the licence plate. Furthermore, Italian licence plates also have blue strips on both sides, however Italian front plates are distinctly shorter.
clues.summary: Plates have either a single red strip on the left or blue strips on both sides. Red on the left is unique in Europe. Italian plates also have blue on both sides, but the front plates are clearly shorter.

differs.how: Italian front plates are distinctly shorter

clues.title: Google car: low Gen 4 with big round blur
text: All Generation 4 coverage in Albania was taken using a “smallcam” camera, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.
NOTE: Most of the Balkans and southern Europe have Smallcam.

images.caption: Four views of the same road: panned down, back, front and a good front blur

clues.summary: A Gen 4 camera mounted lower than usual, with a fairly big round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be see-through and hard to spot. Much of the Balkans and southern Europe has it.

clues.title: Google car: sky rifts from poor stitching
text: ‘**Rifts**’ can rarely be seen in Albanian generation 3 coverage, due to poor stitching.
NOTE: Rifts are also equally common in Montenegro, and can rarely be seen in various other countries.
clues.summary: Rarely, Gen 3 coverage shows odd breaks in the sky where the images were badly stitched together. Montenegro has them just as often.

clues.title: Bollard: black top, red reflector
text: Albanian bollards have a **black top** with a red and grey reflector. The bottom is painted white.
NOTE: Italy uses the same kind of bollards.
clues.summary: White post with a black top and a red-and-grey reflector. Same as Italy, so it narrows it to Albania or Italy.

clues.title: Pole: upside-down triangle top
text: These pole tops, with an **upside down triangle** shape, are a good clue for Albania.
NOTE: Serbia, Czechia, Slovakia and Romania use similar pole tops.
clues.summary: Poletop shaped like an upside-down triangle. Serbia, Czechia, Slovakia and Romania use similar tops, so check other clues.

clues.title: Pole: simple top with horizontal bars
text: Other, more simple Albanian pole tops will often have **horizontal bars**.
NOTE: If you are not sure between Montenegro or Albania and see these poles, guess Albania.
clues.summary: Simpler poletops with horizontal bars. If you can't pick between Albania and Montenegro, guess Albania.

clues.title: Chevron: white on black
text: Albanian chevrons are **white on black**.
NOTE: Within southern Europe this chevron is also used by Italy, Greece, and Spain.
Montenegro uses two chevrons, both of which are different from the Albanian chevron: black on white and red on yellow.
clues.summary: White arrows on black chevrons. Italy, Greece and Spain use the same. Montenegro uses two different ones: black on white and red on yellow.

differs.how: Montenegro uses black on white or red on yellow

clues.title: Sign: backs of road signs painted black
text: The backs of road signs are often painted **black**.
NOTE: This is also common in Italy and Romania.
clues.summary: The backs of road signs are often painted black. Italy and Romania do this too.

clues.title: Stop sign: S with short, angled ends
text: The “S” on Albanian stop signs feature a **distinct shape**; the ends of the S are quite short and have the same angle as the middle, rather than being vertical. This is also sometimes seen on [directional signs](https://www.google.com/maps/@41.4762807,19.7144537,3a,15y,293.79h,86.16t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1s0Xem3meAWDPpNUbSfeuE5A!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu).
NOTE: Italian [stops signs](https://goo.gl/maps/366KjYZAnUyXk4YZ6) and [directional signs](https://goo.gl/maps/EKJL6bTozCYSMke28) have the same feature.

images.caption: Stop sign on the road; the red circle zooms in on the letter S, which has short, angled ends

clues.summary: The S on stop signs has short ends at the same angle as the middle, instead of vertical ends. Direction signs sometimes have it too. Italian stop and direction signs share this.

clues.title: Sign: speed limit with bold numbers
text: The numbers on speed signs are written in a **bold font**.
NOTE: The font is much thinner on speed signs in [Montenegro](https://goo.gl/maps/fvWn6neYoBsnP6J18).
clues.summary: The numbers on speed limit signs are written in a bold font. Montenegro's are much thinner.

differs.how: Montenegrin speed signs use a much thinner font

clues.title: Guardrail: flat wide ends bending away
text: These **flat and wide** guardrail endings that bend away from the road can often be found in Albania.
NOTE: The same endings are found in Italy.
clues.summary: Flat, wide guardrail ends that bend away from the road are common. Italy has the same ends.

clues.title: Language: letters Ë and Ç
text: **Albanian** is not very closely related to any other European languages, and therefore has a fairly distinct look.
Words often contain the letter Ë, ë, and sometimes Ç ç.

images.caption: Albanian text with the letters Ë and Ç shown large

clues.summary: Albanian is not closely related to other European languages, so it looks distinct. Words often have the letter Ë and sometimes Ç. Kosovo uses it too.

clues.title: Sign: street word "rruga"
text: The Albanian word for street is **rruga**.

images.caption: Street name plate reading RRUGA, Albanian for street

clues.summary: The Albanian word for street is rruga.

clues.title: Landscape: green mountains
text: Albania is generally a **mountainous** country, with a **Mediterranean** climate and vegetation. In between the hills and mountains, you can sometimes find more flat, agricultural valleys. The mountains are usually quite green, sometimes with patches of exposed rock visible.
clues.summary: Mostly mountainous with a Mediterranean climate and plants. Flat farming valleys sit between the hills. Mountains are usually green with patches of bare rock.

clues.title: Roadside: lots of exposed red soil
text: Albania has a lot of **exposed red soil** next to roads.
NOTE: This is less common in Montenegro. Greece on the other hand also has a fair amount of similar-looking red soil, especially closer to the Albanian border.
clues.summary: Plenty of bare red soil beside the road. Less common in Montenegro. Greece has similar soil, especially near the Albanian border.

differs.how: Red roadside soil is less common there

clues.title: Houses: cylinder water tanks on roofs
text: You will see a lot of **cylinder-shaped water tanks** on the roofs of buildings.
NOTE: This is less common in Montenegro.
Some parts of Turkey also have a lot of similar-looking water tanks.

images.caption: A cylindrical water tank on a stand on a roof

clues.summary: Lots of cylinder-shaped water tanks sit on rooftops. Less common in Montenegro. Parts of Turkey have many similar tanks.

differs.how: Roof water tanks are less common there

clues.title: Houses: Italian-style, pastel
text: Albania has a lot of **Italian-style buildings**: pastel colours, orange tiled roofs, and blocky shapes with lots of balconies.
clues.summary: Many Italian-style buildings: pastel colours, orange tiled roofs, and blocky shapes with lots of balconies.

clues.title: Cars: Mercedes sedans everywhere
text: **Mercedes** is the most popular car brand in Albania, by quite a margin. The specific style of sedan pictured here is particularly common.

images.caption: Silver Mercedes sedan with a large Mercedes logo overlaid at lower left

clues.summary: Mercedes is by far the most popular car brand, and the sedan style shown is especially common.

clues.title: Google car: long antenna with rifts
text: There are two types of car and camera meta in generation 3 Albania:
- Coverage where the Google car has a long antenna and you can see rifts in the sky.
- Coverage where the Google car has a short antenna and there are no rifts visible.

_You can click on the image to enlarge it. You can also use [this Maps layer](https://www.google.com/maps/d/u/0/viewer?ll=41.11823444009704%2C20.361213161801423&mid=1y5ixAA3bq5FNQrDNfpzSF5Hv80K-BkM&z=8) to look at the coverage in more detail (credits to icraig1205)._
clues.summary: Gen 3 has two car versions. One has a long antenna and shows rifts in the sky. The other has a short antenna and no rifts.

clues.title: Landscape: very mountainous, flat in the west
text: Albania is generally a very mountainous country. This map shows the elevation and relief.

- Low-lying areas are mostly concentrated in the west, around Shkodër, Tirana and Vlorë. This part of the country is characterised by agricultural flatlands and low, undulating hills. Note that the highland plateau around Korçë in the southeast is also very flat.
- The highest mountains can be found in the far north and the far south. In places, these mountains can have an almost alpine look.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: Very mountainous. Flat farmland and low hills are mostly in the west, and a flat highland plateau sits in the southeast. The highest, sometimes almost alpine, mountains are in the far north and far south.

clues.title: Landscape: tall jagged bare mountains
text: The road leading into Theth National Park can typically be recognised by the **tall, jagged mountains**, often with bare mountainsides.
clues.summary: On the road into a national park in the north, look for tall, jagged mountains with bare slopes.

clues.title: Landscape: valley with fully bare cliffs
text: The road by the eastern part of the Montenegrin border goes in a valley with tall, **fully exposed cliff sides** along the road.
clues.summary: A road in a valley with tall, completely bare cliff sides along it, near the eastern edge of the Montenegrin border.

clues.title: Landscape: massive mountain with sheer cliff top
text: Maja e Papingut is a **massive mountain** in the south of Albania, with an almost completely vertical cliffside near the top. It can be seen from several nearby roads.
clues.summary: In the south, a huge mountain with an almost vertical cliff near the top, visible from several nearby roads.

clues.title: Landscape: wide, nearly dry river valley
text: A wide, almost **dried out river valley** going southeast to northwest, can be seen along the SH71 between Pishaj and Kokel.

images.caption: Wide river valley with a gravel riverbed beside the road; a compass icon shows the facing direction

clues.summary: A wide, almost dried-out river valley running southeast to northwest, seen along one road in the south.

clues.title: Landscape: big bay with peninsula and small island
text: The large **Bay of Vlorë** can be seen on many parts of the SH4 between Vlorë and Orikum. It can be recognized by the large Karaburun peninsula jutting out into the ocean from the south, and the small Sazan island just to its north.
clues.summary: A large bay with a long peninsula sticking out from the south and a small island just north of it, seen along a coastal road.

clues.title: Landscape: coastal-looking Aleppo pine forest
text: A couple of small roads northwest of Vlorë can be recognised by the very coastal-looking **Aleppo pine forest**.
clues.summary: A couple of small roads in the southwest run through very coastal-looking Aleppo pine forest.

clues.title: Road lines: double outer lines with wide gap
text: On the SH4 between Levan and Tepelenë and right by the Greek border, you may see **double outer road lines** with a wide gap between them.
clues.summary: On one stretch of road near the Greek border you may see double outer lines with a wide gap between them.

clues.title: Guardrail: triple guardrail on a divided highway
text: Albania only has a few divided highways covered on Street View. All of these and how to differentiate them will be covered in the tips below.
The most easily recognisable divided highway is the A1 between Fushë Milot and Thumanë, which is the only one with a **triple guardrail**.

images.caption: Triple guardrail on a divided highway; circle zooms in on the rails

clues.summary: Few divided highways are covered. The easiest to recognise is one section of the A1 highway, the only one divided by a triple guardrail.

clues.title: Median: plain concrete blocks
text: The sections of the SH2 between Durrës and Tirana and of the SH4 between Lushnjë and Rrogozhinë are both divided by **simple concrete blocks**.

images.caption: Plain concrete block median; circle zooms in on the blocks

clues.summary: Two stretches of highway are divided by simple concrete blocks.

clues.title: Median: concrete blocks with grass between
text: In Tirana, Durrës and on the A3 and SH3 south of Tirana you can find highways which are divided by concrete blocks, with **grass and greenery **in between.

images.caption: Concrete blocks with grass between; circle zooms in on the median

clues.summary: Some highways around the big cities and south of the capital are divided by concrete blocks with grass and greenery between them.

clues.title: Guardrail: basic double guardrail, flat land
text: Most of the SH4 between Durrës and Fier is divided by a **basic double guardrail**. The road does not go through any mountains.

images.caption: Basic double guardrail on flat land; circle zooms in on the rails

clues.summary: A divided road with a plain double guardrail, running through flat land with no mountains.

clues.title: Guardrail: basic double guardrail through mountains
text: The E851 is the only divided road with a basic double guardrail that goes directly **through mountains**.

NOTE: A section of the A3 goes through the mountains but is either divided by a double guardrail with a [fence](https://goo.gl/maps/sEhkf36gQT4r56yMA) above, or with [concrete blocks](https://goo.gl/maps/59RXBrWohChLHePS9).
clues.summary: The only divided road with a plain double guardrail that goes directly through mountains. A mountain section of another highway has a fence above its guardrail or concrete blocks instead.

clues.title: Guardrail: double with extra-tall fence, flat
text: The A2 north of Vlorë can be recognised by the fairly flat surroundings combined with the double guardrail with an **extra tall fence** dividing the highway.

images.caption: Double guardrail with an extra-tall fence; circle zooms in on the rails

clues.summary: A highway in fairly flat land, divided by a double guardrail topped with an extra-tall fence.

clues.title: Landscape: old castle on a tall hill
text: The city of Lezhë can often be recognised by the **old castle** at the top of a tall hill.

images.caption: Town below green hills; the circle at top left magnifies the hill behind the buildings

clues.summary: A town you can often recognise by an old castle at the top of a tall hill.

clues.title: Landscape: town on west side of a wide valley
text: Gjirokaster is a city situated on the **western hillside** of a wide valley.

images.caption: Busy town street with market stalls under trees; a compass icon shows the facing direction

clues.summary: A town built on the western hillside of a wide valley.

clues.title: Landscape: big mountain range to the east
text: Tiranë has a big mountain range in the east, combined with gen 3 and double blue stripes on the license plates, 100% Tiranë.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: The capital has a large mountain range to its east. Combined with Gen 3 coverage and plates with blue strips on both sides, it is a sure sign.
